To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the strike probabilities of grounded rods with different tips in competition tests under switching impulse voltages are determined by two discharge processes.
the strike point is decided by two processes, namely, free development and interception.

(1) the attachment processes in the competition tests are decided by the free development of downward-propagating discharges and the interception process between upward and downward discharging; and (2) for the interception process, the strike probability reflects the different performances of different grounded rods for intercept downward discharges.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the attachment processes of natural lightning strikes and the influencing factors involved.
the influence of the downward leader on the selection of the strike point.
the attachment process of lightning discharges and the influencing factors in competition tests.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the strike probability for a lightning rod depends on the performance of the downward leader, the performance of the lightning rod for intercepting downward leaders, and the scale of the lightning discharge gap, which is determined by the rod height, the height of the lightning current source and the lightning current.
the strike probability is a function of the discharge gap length and the tip characteristics of the grounded rods, and it is not a function of their heights.
the strike point is determined by the competition between the downward leader development and the interception of the downward leader by the grounded rods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, in the case of a rod-rod configuration, the strike probabilities of the rods depend on the relative performances of the rods for intercepting the downward leader, and the relative performances of rods for intercepting a downward leader are mainly determined by the tip shape.
the attachment processes are mainly influenced by the discharge gap, the rod heights and the lightning currents.
the attachment process of natural lightning strikes is similar to the competition process in the competition tests.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the strike probability is a function of the tip shape, the tip radius, and the rod height.
, in order to evaluate the performance of lightning protection systems, it is necessary to take the attachment processes into account.
the attachment processes in a rod-rod competition test depend on the relative scale of the downward-propagation process and the interception process.
